issues.description: Error path swallows server errors silently instead of failing the stream
issues.detail: Known error message_types (auth_error, quota_exceeded, transcriber_error, input_error, error) are detected but the handler appears to only log them. A transcriber telling you 'your audio is wrong' or 'your auth is dead' is not a debug-level event. Either raise APIStatusError and trigger reconnect, or surface it on the event channel. Silently continuing is hostile to the operator.

issues.description: tasks_group.exception() called on a cancelled gather without awaiting
issues.detail: After gracefully_cancel, the code calls tasks_group.cancel() then tasks_group.exception() to suppress the warning. On a cancelled Future, .exception() raises CancelledError. The comment says 'Retrieve exception to prevent it from being logged' but this pattern is wrong shape. Either await it in a try/except or drop the line. As written it can mask reconnect logic.

issues.description: audio_format derived by string interpolation with no validation against STTAudioFormat
issues.detail: `f"pcm_{sample_rate}"` then cast to STTAudioFormat. Pass sample_rate=12345 and you get 'pcm_12345' shipped to the server. The Literal type exists precisely to enumerate valid values; bypassing it with typing.cast is a lie to the type system. Validate against the allowed set or accept STTAudioFormat directly.

issues.description: STTv2 duplicates STT instead of being a mode of it
issues.detail: This is the Deepgram-pattern excuse and it's THREE-PATCHES territory dressed as backward compat. A v2 class with its own SpeechStreamv2, its own option dataclass, and its own __init__ that mostly mirrors v1 means the maintainer-six-years-from-now fixes every bug twice. If the wire protocol genuinely diverges, fine, but justify it in the commit message with the specific shared surface that couldn't be unified.

issues.description: _recognize_impl raises NotImplementedError instead of using base capability flag
issues.detail: STTCapabilities has fields for a reason. If the v2 endpoint is streaming-only, model that in capabilities and let the base class refuse the call cleanly. Raising NotImplementedError from a public method the framework calls is the wrong shape; callers expecting graceful degradation get a stacktrace.

issues.description: No tests, and 'the tests are broken' is not a defense
issues.detail: 'Deepgram v2 also shipped without tests' is the worst possible argument in a review. The pattern compounds. Even one offline test that mocks the WebSocket and asserts START_OF_SPEECH/INTERIM/FINAL/END sequencing on a canned message stream would catch the speaking-state-machine bugs that this code is going to grow. Add it now, while the author still remembers the protocol.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The patch is the right general shape for a streaming WebSocket STT, follows the existing Cartesia/Deepgram voice of the codebase, and the diff is mostly readable. But the error-handling branch for server-side errors is truncated/silent, the audio_format is built by string interpolation and cast past the Literal, and the v2/v1 split is justified by 'Deepgram did it' rather than a real protocol divergence. Fix the error propagation, validate the format, and add at least one mocked-stream test before this lands.
